goals: Oʻzimni tanishtira olaman: kimligim, kasbim va qayerda ishlashim haqida tabiiy gapira olaman.
Present Simple va tez-tezlik ravishlari (always, usually, sometimes, never) yordamida kun tartibimni aytib bera olaman.
He/she/it bilan feʼlga -s qoʻshishni hamda "be" feʼlini (am/is/are) xatosiz ishlata olaman.

ex.q: Dilnoza ___ in the sales department.
ex.why: Dilnoza = she, shuning uchun feʼlga -s qoʻshiladi: works. Oʻzbekchada har bir shaxsning oʻz qoʻshimchasi bor, inglizchada esa faqat he/she/it bilan -s keladi.

ex.q: ___ you work on Saturdays?
ex.why: Gapda asosiy feʼl (work) bor, demak soʻroq Do/Does bilan yasaladi; you bilan Do keladi. Are faqat "be" asosiy feʼl boʻlganda ishlatiladi: Are you busy?

ex.q: I ___ an accountant at a university.
ex.why: Kasbni aytganda "be" feʼli kerak: I am (I'm) an accountant. Oʻzbekchada "Men buxgalterman" feʼlsiz aytiladi, inglizchada esa am tushib qolmasligi kerak.

ex.q: He ___ lunch at his desk.
ex.why: Tez-tezlik ravishi asosiy feʼldan oldin turadi, he bilan esa feʼlga -s qoʻshiladi: usually eats. Feʼl bilan toʻldiruvchi (eats lunch) orasiga ravish qoʻyilmaydi.

ex.q: ___ your boss usually in the office on Fridays?
ex.why: Bu gapda asosiy feʼl yoʻq, faqat joy aytilgan (in the office), shuning uchun "be" kerak: your boss = he/she → Is. Does boʻlishi uchun gapda work kabi asosiy feʼl boʻlishi kerak edi.

a: has
ex.q: Our department ___ (have) a team meeting every Monday.
ex.why: Our department = it, have feʼlining 3-shaxs birlikdagi shakli esa has (haves emas). every Monday — takrorlanadigan ish, shuning uchun Present Simple.

a: doesn't drink
does not drink
ex.q: He ___ (not / drink) coffee after lunch.
ex.why: He bilan inkor doesn't orqali yasaladi, undan keyin feʼl -s siz qoladi: doesn't drink. -s allaqachon does ichida bor.

a: does your boss travel
ex.q: How often ___ (your boss / travel) for work?
ex.why: Soʻroqda tartib: soʻroq soʻz + does + ega + feʼlning asl shakli. Oʻzbekchada soʻroq -mi yoki ohang bilan yasaladi, inglizchada esa does eganing oldiga qoʻyiladi va feʼl -s olmaydi.

ex.a: My manager is always late for meetings.
ex.why: "be" feʼli bilan tez-tezlik ravishi undan KEYIN keladi: is always late. Oddiy feʼllarda esa ravish feʼldan oldin turadi (always works).

ex.a: Does your brother usually drive to work?
ex.why: Soʻroq tartibi: Does + ega + ravish + feʼlning asl shakli. Does ishlatilgani uchun drive -s olmaydi.

a: My coworker Dave lives near the office.
ex.q: My coworker Dave live near the office.
ex.why: Dave = he, shuning uchun feʼl -s oladi: lives. Ega ism yoki ot boʻlsa ham (Dave, my coworker), qoida he/she/it bilan bir xil.

a: Do you usually work from home on Fridays?
ex.q: Are you usually work from home on Fridays?
ex.why: Gapda asosiy feʼl work bor, shuning uchun soʻroq Do bilan boshlanadi. Are faqat "be" asosiy feʼl boʻlgan gaplarda keladi (Are you at home?); are va work yonma-yon kelmaydi.

a: Sardor doesn't work on Saturdays.
Sardor does not work on Saturdays.
Sardor doesn't work Saturdays.
Sardor does not work Saturdays.
ex.why: Odat haqidagi inkor: he/she/it bilan doesn't + feʼlning asl shakli (works emas). "Shanba kunlari" — on Saturdays: har shanba nazarda tutilgani uchun koʻplikda.

a: I'm usually busy on Mondays.
I am usually busy on Mondays.
Usually I'm busy on Mondays.
Usually I am busy on Mondays.
On Mondays I'm usually busy.
On Mondays I am usually busy.
ex.uz: Men dushanba kunlari odatda band boʻlaman.
ex.why: "Band boʻlaman" — holat, shuning uchun "be" kerak: I'm busy. Tez-tezlik ravishi "be" dan keyin turadi: I'm usually busy (I usually busy emas).

grammar.intro: Present Simple — odatlar, takrorlanib turadigan ishlar va oʻzgarmas faktlar zamoni. Oʻzingiz, ishingiz va kun tartibingiz haqida gapirganda amerikaliklar deyarli faqat shu zamondan foydalanadi. Bugun uning eng koʻp xato qilinadigan joylarini takrorlaymiz: he/she/it bilan -s, do/does bilan inkor va soʻroq, "be" feʼli hamda always, usually kabi soʻzlarning gapdagi oʻrni.

mistakes.why: My manager = he yoki she, shuning uchun feʼlga -s qoʻshiladi. Ingliz tilida qoʻshimcha faqat shu shaxsda borligi uchun u eng koʻp unutiladi.
doesn't dan keyin feʼl asl shaklda turadi. -s bir gapda faqat bir marta keladi va u allaqachon does ichida bor.
Odat va faktlarda am/is/are oddiy feʼl bilan birga ishlatilmaydi. Yo "be" (I'm an accountant), yo asosiy feʼl (I work) — ikkalasi birga emas.

mistakes.bad: I check always my email first.
mistakes.good: I always check my email first.
mistakes.why: always, usually, never kabi ravishlar asosiy feʼldan oldin turadi. Feʼl bilan uning toʻldiruvchisi (check my email) orasiga hech narsa qoʻyilmaydi.

ex.en: I work in the finance department.
She works at a bank.
Aziz has a meeting every Monday.
ex.uz: Azizning har dushanba kuni yigʻilishi boʻladi.

points.h: Odat va faktlar: I work / she works
points.text: Har doim, odatda yoki muntazam boʻladigan ishlar va oʻzgarmas faktlar Present Simple bilan aytiladi. I, you, we, they bilan feʼl oʻzgarmaydi, he, she, it bilan esa feʼlga -s yoki -es qoʻshiladi (works, goes, watches; have → has). Oʻzbek tilida har bir shaxsning oʻz qoʻshimchasi bor (ishlayman, ishlaysan, ishlaydi), ingliz tilida esa qoʻshimcha faqat 3-shaxs birlikda keladi — shuning uchun u oson unutiladi.

ex.en: I don't work on weekends.
He doesn't drink coffee.
Does she work with you?

points.h: Inkor va soʻroq: don't / doesn't, do / does
points.text: Inkor gapda don't (he/she/it bilan doesn't), soʻroq gapda esa gap boshida Do yoki Does ishlatiladi. Does yoki doesn't dan keyin asosiy feʼl -s siz, asl shaklda qoladi, chunki -s allaqachon does ichida bor. Oʻzbek tilida soʻroq -mi qoʻshimchasi bilan yasaladi, ingliz tilida esa Do/Does ni gap boshiga qoʻyish shart.

ex.en: I'm an accountant.
My office is downtown.
Are you busy right now?

points.text: Ism, kasb, yosh, holat va joy haqida gapirganda "be" feʼli kerak: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're. Oʻzbek tilida "Men buxgalterman" yoki "U band" deganda alohida feʼl yoʻq, ingliz tilida esa am/is/are tushib qolsa, gap xato boʻladi. Inkor: I'm not, he isn't, they aren't. Soʻroqda "be" gap boshiga chiqadi (Are you busy?) va bunda do/does ishlatilmaydi.

ex.en: I usually get to work at 8:30.
She's always on time.
ex.uz: U har doim oʻz vaqtida keladi.

ex.en: He never takes a lunch break.
ex.uz: U hech qachon tushlik tanaffusiga chiqmaydi.

points.h: Tez-tezlik ravishlari: always, usually, often, sometimes, never
points.text: Bu soʻzlar ish qanchalik tez-tez boʻlishini bildiradi: always (har doim) → usually (odatda) → often (tez-tez) → sometimes (baʼzan) → hardly ever (deyarli hech qachon) → never (hech qachon). Ular asosiy feʼldan OLDIN turadi (I usually get up at six), lekin "be" feʼlidan KEYIN keladi (I'm usually busy). never soʻzining oʻzi inkor maʼnosini beradi, shuning uchun u bilan don't ishlatilmaydi: I never eat breakfast.

ex.en: I go to the gym twice a week.
ex.uz: Men haftasiga ikki marta sport zaliga boraman.

ex.en: How often do you work from home?
We have a team meeting every Monday.
ex.uz: Har dushanba kuni jamoa yigʻilishimiz boʻladi.

points.text: every day, on Mondays, once a week, twice a month kabi iboralar odatda gap oxirida keladi. Ish qanchalik tez-tez boʻlishini soʻrash uchun "How often do you ...?" deyiladi. Ingliz gapida tartib qatʼiy: ega + feʼl + toʻldiruvchi + joy + vaqt; oʻzbek tilidagi kabi feʼlni gap oxiriga qoʻyib boʻlmaydi.

lines.t: Hi, I'm Sarah. Are you here for the finance workshop?
Yeah, I am. I'm Aziz. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too. So, what do you do, Aziz?
I'm an accountant. I work in the finance department at a university in Tashkent.
Oh, nice. What's that like?
It's busy. I deal with invoices and budgets all day. What about you?
I work for a small tech company in Denver. I'm in charge of payroll.
So everyone gets paid on time because of you.
Usually! Do you start work early?
Pretty early. I get up at six, and I get to work around eight.
Wow. I'm never at my desk before nine. I always grab a coffee first.
Me too. I can't work without coffee.
What do you usually do after work?
I usually head home and hang out with my kids. On weekends we sometimes go to the mountains.
That sounds great.

reading.text:
Madina is 34 years old. She's an accountant, and she works for a small trading company in Tashkent. She's in charge of payments, so she deals with invoices and bank transfers every day.

Madina usually gets up at 6:00. She makes breakfast for her two kids and takes them to school. She gets to work around 8:30, and she's almost never late. Her boss, Mike, is from Chicago. He's friendly, but he's always busy, and he doesn't like long meetings.

Mornings are usually quiet at the office. Madina checks her email, pays the bills, and updates her spreadsheets. Around 11:00 she takes a short break and grabs a coffee with her coworker Nigora. They often talk about their kids and their weekend plans.

The end of the month is different. Everyone gets paid on the 30th, so Madina is really busy that week. She sometimes stays at the office until 7:00.

After work, Madina heads home and has dinner with her family. She doesn't watch much TV. She's really into books, and she usually reads for half an hour before bed.

tips: Present Simple ishlating: I work ..., I usually ..., I'm in charge of ...
Kamida uchta tez-tezlik ravishini qoʻshing: always, usually, sometimes, never.
Bugungi iboralardan kamida uchtasini ishlating, masalan: deal with, get to work, head home.
writing.uz: AQShdan kelgan yangi hamkasbingizga oʻzingizni tanishtirib qisqa xabar yozing: kimligingiz, nima ish qilishingiz va odatdagi kuningiz qanday oʻtishi haqida.

goals: Ayni paytda qilayotgan ishim haqida Present Continuous bilan gapira olaman: I'm working on ...
Vaqtinchalik va oʻzgarayotgan holatlarni tasvirlay olaman (this week, these days, getting better).
Telefonda qisqa, tabiiy suhbat qura olaman: Is this a good time? Can I call you back?

ex.q: Jasur can't come to the phone. He ___ to a client.
ex.why: Ayni shu paytda boʻlayotgan ish — Present Continuous: he + is + talking. "be" siz faqat talking deyish xato, chunki oʻzbekchadagi -yap- oʻrnini inglizchada is + -ing birgalikda beradi.

ex.q: What ___ you working on today?
ex.why: Present Continuous soʻrogʻida yordamchi feʼl — "be": you bilan are. do va does faqat Present Simple da ishlatiladi, ulardan keyin -ing kelmaydi.

ex.q: Take my laptop. I ___ it right now.
ex.why: Inkor am/is/are + not + -ing bilan yasaladi: I am not (I'm not) using. don't dan keyin -ing kelmaydi, isn't esa he/she/it uchun.

ex.q: Gas prices ___ up again.
ex.why: Prices — koʻplikdagi ot (they), shuning uchun are going. Narxning oshishi kabi asta-sekin oʻzgarayotgan holatlar Present Continuous bilan aytiladi.

ex.q: Why ___ so early today?
ex.why: Soʻroq soʻzdan keyin tartib: is + ega + -ing. Oʻzbekchada soʻroq gapda soʻz tartibi oʻzgarmaydi, inglizchada esa is eganing oldiga oʻtadi; does bilan -ing ishlatilmaydi.

ex.why: Hozir davom etayotgan ish: my boss = he/she, demak is + waiting. Faqat waiting yozish yetarli emas — "be" albatta kerak.

grammar.intro: Present Continuous (am/is/are + feʼl-ing) ayni gapirayotgan paytda yoki shu kunlarda davom etayotgan, hali tugamagan ishlarni bildiradi. Telefonda, yozishmalarda va ishda "hozir nima qilyapsan?" degan savolga amerikaliklar aynan shu zamon bilan javob beradi. U oʻzbek tilidagi -yap- qoʻshimchasiga (ishlayapman) toʻgʻri keladi, lekin ingliz tilida ikki qism kerak: "be" + -ing.

mistakes.bad: I working on the budget now.
mistakes.good: I'm working on the budget now.
mistakes.why: -ing dan oldin am/is/are boʻlishi shart. Oʻzbekchadagi -yap- qoʻshimchasi inglizchada ikki qismga boʻlinadi: "be" + -ing.

mistakes.bad: She is work from home today.
mistakes.why: Bu zamonda "be" dan keyin feʼl asl shaklda qolmaydi, unga -ing qoʻshiladi: is working.
write feʼli -e bilan tugaydi: -e tushadi, lekin undosh ikkilanmaydi (writing). Undosh faqat sit → sitting, get → getting kabi qisqa feʼllarda ikkilanadi.
Present Continuous inkori "be" + not bilan yasaladi. don't va doesn't faqat Present Simple da ishlatiladi: I don't work on Sundays.

ex.en: I'm working on the monthly report.

points.text: Bu zamon ikki qismdan iborat: "be" feʼli (am/is/are) va -ing qoʻshilgan feʼl. Ogʻzaki nutqda deyarli har doim qisqartma ishlatiladi: I'm, you're, he's, she's, we're, they're. Oʻzbekchada bitta soʻz (ishlayapman) yetarli boʻlgani uchun "be" koʻp tushib qoladi: "I working" emas, "I'm working".

ex.en: I'm writing an email.
We're running late.
He's getting ready for a meeting.

points.text: Koʻpchilik feʼllarga shunchaki -ing qoʻshiladi: work → working, check → checking. Feʼl -e bilan tugasa, -e tushib qoladi: make → making, write → writing. Qisqa feʼl bitta unli + bitta undosh bilan tugasa, oxirgi undosh ikkilanadi: run → running, sit → sitting, get → getting.

ex.en: I'm not doing anything right now.
Is she coming to the meeting?
What are you looking for?

points.text: Inkorda "be" dan keyin not qoʻyiladi: I'm not, he isn't, they aren't. Soʻroqda "be" eganing oldiga chiqadi: Are you working? What are you doing? Bu zamonda do, does, don't ishlatilmaydi — yordamchi feʼl vazifasini "be" bajaradi.

ex.en: I'm working from home this week.
My sister is staying with us this week.

Hi Madina,

We're closing the books for the year, so everyone in the finance department is working late. Right now I'm sitting at my desk with a cold coffee and about forty invoices. Talk soon,
Rachel

reading.text:
Dilnoza works for a small company that sells kitchen equipment to restaurants and cafes. She's an accountant. On a typical day, she deals with invoices, pays suppliers, and keeps track of everything the company spends. She usually gets to the office at 8:30 and leaves around 5:30.

But this isn't a typical month. The company is growing fast. It's opening a second store in Samarkand, and it's hiring ten new people. So these days Dilnoza is doing two jobs. She's still doing the accounting, and she's also helping her boss, Mike, plan the budget for the new store. This week she's staying at the office until 7 every night.

Dilnoza doesn't mind. She likes her job, and she gets along with her coworkers. She also knows it's only for a few months. "Mike wants to hire another accountant," she says. "He's looking for somebody at the moment. I think that makes sense. We need the help!"

For now, she's drinking a lot of coffee and trying to cut costs wherever she can. Mike likes that, too.

grammar.intro: Suhbatni savollar olib boradi: yangi odam bilan tanishganda gapning yarmi savoldan iborat boʻladi. Oʻzbek tilida savol tuzish oson — gap tartibi oʻzgarmaydi, faqat -mi qoʻshiladi yoki soʻroq soʻzi qoʻyiladi. Ingliz tilida esa yordamchi feʼl (do/does, am/is/are) kerak va u egadan oldinga chiqadi; eng koʻp xato aynan shu yerda qilinadi.

mistakes.why: Oʻzbekcha «Qayerda ishlaysiz?» gapida yordamchi feʼl yoʻq, shuning uchun do tushib qoladi. Inglizcha savolda ega (you) oldidan do/does turishi shart.
this — gapning egasi, mean — asosiy feʼl. Savolda egadan oldin does kerak, asosiy feʼl esa egadan keyin, qoʻshimchasiz keladi.
Who bu yerda gapning egasi (kim ishlaydi?). Ega haqidagi savolda do/does qoʻyilmaydi, -s esa feʼlning oʻziga qoʻshiladi.

mistakes.bad: A: Do you like your job? B: Yes, I like.
mistakes.good: A: Do you like your job? B: Yes, I do.
mistakes.why: Oʻzbekchada «Ha, yoqadi» deb asosiy feʼl takrorlanadi, inglizchada esa yordamchi feʼl: Yes, I do. like dan keyin toʻldiruvchi boʻlmasa, gap tugallanmagan boʻlib qoladi.

points.h: Yes/no savollar: yordamchi feʼl + ega + feʼl
points.text: Oʻzbekchada gap tartibi oʻzgarmaydi, faqat -mi qoʻshiladi: «Siz shu yerda ishlaysizmi?» Inglizchada -mi vazifasini gap boshiga chiqadigan do/does bajaradi, asosiy feʼl esa qoʻshimchasiz qoladi: Do you work here? Does she work here? be feʼli (am/is/are) va Present Continuous bilan do kerak emas — am/is/are ning oʻzi egadan oldinga oʻtadi: Are you busy? Is he working?

points.text: Faqat «Yes» yoki «No» deyish quruq va biroz qoʻpol eshitiladi. Oʻzbekchada «Ha, ishlayman» deb asosiy feʼlni takrorlaymiz, inglizchada esa savoldagi yordamchi feʼl takrorlanadi: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. / Yes, she is. / No, they aren't. «Yes» li qisqa javobda qisqartma ishlatilmaydi: Yes, I am (Yes, I'm emas).

points.h: Wh- savollar: soʻroq soʻzi + yordamchi feʼl + ega + feʼl
points.text: What, where, when, why, how, how much, how many, what kind of — soʻroq soʻzi gap boshida turadi, undan keyin yes/no savol tartibi keladi. Oʻzbekcha «Siz qayerda yashaysiz?» gapida yordamchi feʼl yoʻq, shuning uchun inglizchada ham do tushib qoladi: Where you live? Toʻgʻrisi: Where do you live?

ex.en: Who helps you at work?
Who do you help at work?
Which bus goes downtown?

points.h: Ega haqidagi savol: do/does kerak emas
points.text: Agar who, what yoki which + ot gapning egasini soʻrasa (kim qiladi? nima boʻladi?), do/does qoʻyilmaydi, soʻz tartibi darak gapdagidek qoladi va feʼl 3-shaxs birlikda (-s bilan) keladi: Who helps you? Agar toʻldiruvchi soʻralsa (kimga? nimani?), do/does kerak: Who do you help? Oʻzbekchada bu farqni kelishik qoʻshimchasi koʻrsatadi (kim? — kimga? kimni?), inglizchada esa soʻz tartibi va do/does.

ex.en: Who do you live with?
What are you looking for?
What's your new boss like?

points.text: Ogʻzaki inglizchada predlog (with, for, from, about, to) savol oxirida qoladi: Who do you live with? Where are you from? What are you looking for? With whom...? shakli juda rasmiy, kundalik nutqda deyarli ishlatilmaydi. Yana bir foydali savol — What is ... like? (ogʻzaki nutqda what's ... like?): «... qanaqa?» degani; bu yerda like «yoqtirmoq» emas.

lines.t: Excuse me, is anybody sitting here?
No, go ahead. I'm Jasur, by the way.
I'm Rachel. Nice to meet you. So, what do you do for a living?
I'm an accountant. I work for a construction company. How about you?
I teach English at a language school. Are you from Tashkent?
Actually, no. I'm originally from Bukhara. Where are you from?
Seattle. I'm here for a year.
Oh, nice. How do you like Tashkent so far?
I love it. The food is amazing. Hey, who teaches this class?
Dave does. He's really good.
Great. So what do you do in your free time?
I'm really into soccer. I play every Sunday. Do you play any sports?
No, I don't. But I love hiking.
Really? Me too! We have a lot in common.

q.why: Rachel sport bilan shugʻullanmaydi, lekin «I love hiking» deydi; Jasur esa «Me too» deb javob beradi.

reading.text:
It's Madina's first day at her new job, and she has a lot of questions. Where does she sit? Who does she report to? What time does everybody go to lunch?

Josh, a friendly guy from her team, shows her around the office. "Who's your manager?" he asks.

"Sarah Miller," Madina says. "What's she like?"

"She's great. She actually listens to people. By the way, are you from Tashkent?"

"No, I'm not. I'm originally from Fergana. How about you? Where are you from?"

"Denver. My wife works at the university here, so we're living in Tashkent for now."

At noon, Josh takes her to the cafe downstairs. "Who makes the best coffee around here?" Madina asks.

"This place does. But they charge a lot for it!"

They talk about work, family, and music. They're both into jazz, and they both have two kids. "We have a lot in common," Madina thinks.

"So, how do you like it so far?" Josh asks after lunch.

"So far, I love it," she says. "But ask me again in a month!"

It's a good first day. Madina wants to get to know everybody on her team.

tips: Har bir savolda yordamchi feʼl borligini tekshiring: do/does yoki am/is/are egadan oldin turishi kerak.
Kamida bitta ega haqidagi savol yozing (masalan, Who cooks ...?) — unda do/does boʻlmaydi.
Predlogni savol oxiriga qoʻying: Who do you live with? What are you into?
writing.uz: Internetda Mike ismli yangi til oʻrganish sherigingiz bor. Unga birinchi xabar yozing: oʻzingizni ikki gapda tanishtiring va 5–6 ta savol bering (yes/no, wh- va kamida bitta ega haqidagi savol).

goals: "there's / there are" yordamida ofisingizda, uyingizda va atrofda nima borligini ayta olasiz.
Miqdorni toʻgʻri ifodalay olasiz: some / any, much / many / a lot of, a few / a little.
"money", "information", "advice" kabi sanalmaydigan otlarni xatosiz ishlata olasiz.

ex.q: ___ any good restaurants near your office?
ex.why: "restaurants" koʻplikda, shuning uchun "Are there" kerak; savolda "are" "there" dan oldinga oʻtadi. "Are they" esa "ular ...mi?" degani, "bormi?" emas.

ex.q: There ___ a lot of traffic this morning.
ex.why: "traffic" sanalmaydigan ot, shuning uchun feʼl birlikda: "there is". "a lot of" feʼl shakliga taʼsir qilmaydi — undan keyingi otga qaraladi.

ex.q: How ___ time do we have before the meeting?
ex.why: "time" (vaqt) sanalmaydi, shuning uchun "How much". "How many" faqat koʻplikdagi sanaladigan otlar bilan keladi.

ex.q: Sorry, I don't have ___ cash on me.
ex.why: Inkor gapda ("don't have") "some" emas, "any" ishlatiladi. "cash" sanalmaydigan ot boʻlgani uchun "many" va "a few" ham toʻgʻri kelmaydi.

ex.q: My manager always gives me ___ before a big meeting.
ex.why: "advice" sanalmaydi: oldiga "a" qoʻyilmaydi, oxiriga "-s" qoʻshilmaydi va "many" bilan kelmaydi. Toʻgʻrisi — "some good advice".

a: are
ex.q: Right now there ___ (be) two new people on our team.
ex.why: "two new people" koʻplikda, shuning uchun "there are". Feʼl "there" dan keyin kelgan otga moslashadi.

a: many
ex.q: How ___ (much / many) vacation days do you get a year?
ex.why: "days" sanaladigan ot va koʻplikda turibdi, demak "How many". Oʻzbekchada ikkalasi ham "qancha", inglizchada esa otning turiga qarab tanlanadi.

a: a little
ex.q: Don't worry, I have ___ (a few / a little) money saved up.
ex.why: "money" sanalmaydi, shuning uchun "a little" (biroz). "a few" faqat sanaladigan otlar bilan keladi: "a few dollars".

ex.a: Is there any coffee left in the kitchen?
ex.why: Savolda "is" gap boshiga chiqadi: "Is there...?". "coffee" sanalmaydi, savolda esa "any" ishlatiladi; "left" (qolgan) otdan keyin keladi.

ex.a: I have a few questions about the budget.
ex.uz: Byudjet boʻyicha bir nechta savolim bor.
ex.why: "questions" sanaladigan ot, shuning uchun "a few" (bir nechta). Tartib: ega + feʼl + miqdor + ot + "about ...".

a: There are a lot of people in line at the bank.
ex.q: There is a lot of people in line at the bank.
ex.why: "people" — koʻplikdagi ot ("person" ning koʻpligi), shuning uchun "There are". "a lot of" dan keyingi otga qarab "is" yoki "are" tanlanadi.

a: We need to buy some new furniture for the office.
ex.q: We need to buy some new furnitures for the office.
ex.why: "furniture" (mebel) sanalmaydigan ot, unga koʻplik "-s" qoʻshilmaydi. Bitta buyum haqida "a piece of furniture" deyiladi.

I do not have much money this month.
I don't have a lot of money this month.
I do not have a lot of money this month.
This month I don't have much money.
This month I don't have a lot of money.
ex.why: "money" sanalmaydi, shuning uchun inkor gapda "much" keladi ("many" emas); "a lot of" ham toʻgʻri. "moneys" degan shakl ishlatilmaydi.

a: I need some information about this project.
I need a little information about this project.
I need some info about this project.
I need a little info about this project.
I need a bit of information about this project.
I need a little bit of information about this project.
ex.uz: Menga bu loyiha haqida biroz maʼlumot kerak.
ex.why: "information" sanalmaydi: "an information" yoki "informations" deyilmaydi. "biroz" maʼnosida "some" yoki "a little" ishlatiladi.

grammar.intro: Biror joyda nima borligini aytish uchun amerikaliklar gapni "there's" yoki "there are" bilan boshlaydi, miqdorni esa "some", "any", "a lot of", "a few", "a little" bilan bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilida "pullar", "maʼlumotlar", "maslahatlar" deyish mumkin, ingliz tilida esa bu otlar sanalmaydi — eng koʻp xato aynan shu yerda chiqadi. Bugun shu xatolardan qutulamiz.

mistakes.why: "information" sanalmaydigan ot: koʻplik "-s" olmaydi, "an information" ham deyilmaydi. Oʻzbekchadagi "maʼlumotlar" inglizchada baribir "information" boʻladi.

mistakes.bad: How many money do you have?
mistakes.good: How much money do you have?
mistakes.why: "money" sanalmaydi (dollar yoki soʻm sanaladi, pulning oʻzi emas), shuning uchun "How much" kerak.

mistakes.bad: She gave me a good advice.
mistakes.good: She gave me some good advice.
mistakes.why: "advice" oldiga "a" qoʻyilmaydi, chunki u sanalmaydi. "some advice" yoki bitta maslahat uchun "a piece of advice" deyiladi.

mistakes.good: I have a lot of work today.
mistakes.why: Tasdiq gapda "much" kundalik nutqda gʻalati, kitobiy eshitiladi — amerikaliklar "a lot of" deydi. "much" asosan inkor gapda va savolda ishlatiladi.

ex.en: There's a coffee machine on the second floor.

reading.text:
Jasur is an accountant from Tashkent. This month he's working at his company's office in Chicago. His English is good, but in his first week something feels wrong. His coworkers are friendly, but they look a little surprised when he talks to them.

On Friday, his coworker Rachel says, "Let's grab a coffee." At the coffee shop, Jasur tells the cashier, "I want a black coffee." Rachel smiles. "Can I give you some advice?" she asks. "Your English is great, but 'I want' sounds a little rude here. Say 'Can I get a black coffee, please?' or 'I'd like a black coffee.'"

"What about at work?" Jasur asks. "I usually just say, 'Send me the invoice.'"

"Oh, don't say that!" Rachel laughs. "Try 'Could you send me the invoice?' or 'Would you mind sending me the invoice?' People are happy to do you a favor when you ask nicely."

On Monday, Jasur stops by Dave's desk. "Hey Dave, do you have a second? Could you take a look at these numbers?"

"Sure, no problem," Dave says with a big smile.

Now Jasur knows: in English, politeness is in small words like "can," "could," and "please."

grammar.why: Takror ravishlari (always, usually, never) "be" feʼlidan keyin, boshqa feʼllardan esa oldin keladi: is never late.

grammar.q: ___ your brother work in an office?
grammar.why: He/she/it (your brother) bilan Present Simple soʻroq gapi "does" + feʼlning asosiy shakli bilan tuziladi; "is" bilan "work" birga kelmaydi.

a: I agree with you about the new schedule.
I do agree with you about the new schedule.
grammar.q: I am agree with you about the new schedule.
grammar.why: "Agree" sifat emas, feʼl, shuning uchun Present Simple da "am" qoʻshilmaydi: I agree.

grammar.q: Dave can't come to the phone. He ___ to a client right now.
grammar.why: "Right now" ayni shu paytda boʻlayotgan ishni bildiradi, shuning uchun Present Continuous kerak: is + -ing.

grammar.why: Oʻzgarib borayotgan vaziyat Present Continuous bilan aytiladi; "prices" koʻplikda, shuning uchun "are going".

grammar.why: "Know" holat feʼli boʻlib, hozirgi payt haqida gapirilsa ham Continuous shaklida ishlatilmaydi.

grammar.q: Rachel usually takes the bus, but today she ___ to work.
grammar.why: Odatdagi ish Present Simple da (usually takes), faqat bugungi, odatdan tashqari ish esa Present Continuous da (is walking) aytiladi.

a: I need your help with this spreadsheet.
grammar.q: I'm needing your help with this spreadsheet.
grammar.why: "Need" holat feʼli, shuning uchun -ing shaklida emas, Present Simple da ishlatiladi: I need.

grammar.why: Savol egaga berilganda (kim imzolaydi?) "do/does" ishlatilmaydi va feʼl darak gapdagidek -s bilan keladi: Who signs...?
Qisqa javobda asosiy feʼl takrorlanmaydi, savoldagi yordamchi feʼl qaytariladi: Does...? - Yes, she does.

grammar.uz: Dam olish kunlari odatda nima qilasiz?
grammar.why: Wh-savolda tartib: soʻroq soʻz + do/does + ega + feʼl; "usually" ega bilan asosiy feʼl orasida turadi.

grammar.why: Wh-savol tartibi: soʻroq soʻz + does + ega + feʼlning asosiy shakli; "does" dan keyin feʼlga -s qoʻshilmaydi.

grammar.why: "Information" sanalmaydigan ot: koʻplik shakli yoʻq va "an" bilan kelmaydi, shuning uchun "some information" deyiladi.

grammar.q: Hurry up! We don't have ___ time before the meeting.
grammar.why: "Time" bu yerda sanalmaydigan ot, inkor gapda u bilan "much" ishlatiladi; "many" va "a few" faqat sanaladigan otlar bilan keladi.

reading.text:
Nigora works in the finance department of a small university. She usually starts at nine and leaves at six. Most of the year, her job is not very stressful. She checks invoices, answers emails and prepares a short report every Friday.

This week is different. The university is closing its books for the year, so everyone in the department is working late. Nigora is checking hundreds of payments, and her coworker Dave is helping her. They are also training a new assistant, Sardor. He doesn't know the system yet, so he asks a lot of questions. Nigora doesn't mind. She remembers her own first month, and she thinks questions are a good sign.

There is a small kitchen next to the office. There are a few snacks in the cabinet, but there isn't much coffee left, and there isn't any milk. "Let's order some food," Dave says at seven. "I'd like pizza. What do you want?" Nigora wants something light, so she asks for a salad. Sardor doesn't want anything. He just needs a little more time with the payment system.

"Could you check these numbers for me?" he asks Nigora. She looks at the screen and smiles. Everything is correct. "Good job," she says. "Now save the file and go home. We have a lot of work tomorrow, too."
reading.title: A Busy Week in the Finance Department
